# Agentic AI Platform Landscape — May 2026

## Part 1: The Dossiers (20 platforms)

### Coding / Dev Agents

**1. Cursor** — [cursor.com](https://cursor.com)
- **Position:** AI-native IDE fork of VS Code with always-on tab + agent.
- **User:** Devs (individual + teams).
- **Pricing:** Hobby $0 / Pro $20 / Pro+ $60 / Ultra $200 / Teams $40 per seat. Credit-based.
- **Killer feature:** Tab autocomplete that predicts multi-line edits across files; best-in-class latency.
- **Hero copy:** *"Built to make you extraordinarily productive, Cursor is the best way to code with AI."*
- **Weakness:** Costs spike unpredictably on credit model; weak at long-horizon autonomous tasks vs. Devin/Claude Code.

**2. Windsurf (Codeium)** — [windsurf.com](https://windsurf.com)
- **Position:** "Cascade" agent IDE with hybrid local+cloud execution.
- **User:** Devs, esp. enterprise/regulated.
- **Pricing:** Free 25 credits / Pro $15 / Teams $30 / Enterprise $60+.
- **Killer feature:** Codemaps + SWE-1.5 model; unlimited tab autocomplete on free tier.
- **Hero copy:** *"Where developers are doing their best work. Ship more with local and cloud agents working together."*
- **Weakness:** Brand churn (Codeium → Windsurf → OpenAI acquisition saga); narrower ecosystem than Cursor.

**3. Devin (Cognition)** — [devin.ai](https://devin.ai)
- **Position:** Fully autonomous AI software engineer (Slack-issued tickets, opens PRs).
- **User:** Eng managers, platform teams.
- **Pricing:** Core $20/mo (~$2.25/ACU) → Team $500 → Enterprise custom.
- **Killer feature:** End-to-end ticket → branch → PR with browser + shell + IDE; runs unattended for hours.
- **Hero copy:** *"Devin, the AI software engineer. Build with Devin."*
- **Weakness:** Quality on novel codebases still spotty; ACU billing makes ROI fuzzy.

**4. Claude Code** — [claude.com](https://claude.com)
- **Position:** Terminal-native agent operating directly on your repo.
- **User:** Senior devs, infra teams.
- **Pricing:** Bundled with Pro $20 / Max $100–$200 / Team Premium $100/seat (5-min) / API pay-go.
- **Killer feature:** Direct file/shell/git access in your real environment; subagents + skills + 1M context on Opus.
- **Hero copy:** *"Code at the speed of thought."*
- **Weakness:** No GUI; CLI-first scares non-power-users; usage anxiety on Max plans.

**5. Replit Agent 3** — [replit.com](https://replit.com)
- **Position:** Browser-based "build apps from a prompt" with deploy.
- **User:** Generalist / non-dev builders.
- **Pricing:** Free trial / Core $20 / Pro $100+ teams. Effort-based credits.
- **Killer feature:** 200-min unattended sessions; native deploy + DB + auth in one tab.
- **Hero copy:** *"Turn your ideas into apps."*
- **Weakness:** Quality plateau on serious codebases; effort-pricing produces sticker shock.

### Computer-Use / Web Agents

**6. OpenAI Operator (ChatGPT Agent Mode)** — [openai.com](https://openai.com)
- **Position:** ChatGPT that drives a browser/computer for you.
- **User:** Generalist consumers + ops.
- **Pricing:** Plus $20 (waitlist/limited) / Pro $100–$200/mo.
- **Killer feature:** Bundled into ChatGPT — billions of distribution touchpoints.
- **Hero copy:** *"ChatGPT can now use a computer."*
- **Weakness:** Capped session time; failures are silent; not API-first for developers.

**7. Anthropic Computer Use** — [anthropic.com](https://anthropic.com)
- **Position:** API primitive — let Claude move a mouse and read a screen.
- **User:** Devs building custom agents.
- **Pricing:** API only — Sonnet 4.6 $3/$15 per MTok, Opus 4.7 $5/$25.
- **Killer feature:** Pure API; the most-shipped underlying model behind other people's agents.
- **Hero copy:** *"Claude can now use computers."*
- **Weakness:** Slow vs. native APIs; you build the harness yourself.

**8. Google Project Mariner** — [deepmind.google](https://deepmind.google/models/project-mariner)
- **Position:** Gemini-powered browser agent, now shipping inside Gemini 3 Pro.
- **User:** Google AI Ultra subscribers, devs via Gemini API.
- **Pricing:** Bundled with Google AI Ultra (~$249/mo); API metered.
- **Killer feature:** 10 concurrent cloud-VM tasks; 83.5% WebVoyager.
- **Hero copy:** *"A research prototype exploring the future of human-agent interaction."*
- **Weakness:** Still "research prototype" framing; Google's productization tax.

**9. Manus** — [manus.im](https://manus.im)
- **Position:** General autonomous agent — long-horizon research/build tasks.
- **User:** Generalist knowledge workers.
- **Pricing:** Free 300 daily credits / Pro $20 or $40 / Team $20/seat.
- **Killer feature:** Runs unattended on a VM; ships finished artifacts (decks, sites, reports).
- **Hero copy:** *"What can I do for you? Less structure, more intelligence."*
- **Weakness:** Credit burn on complex tasks; Chinese-origin trust friction in US enterprise.

**10. MultiOn** — [multion.ai](https://multion.ai)
- **Position:** "Motor cortex" API — millions of concurrent web agents on demand.
- **User:** Devs building consumer apps with web actions.
- **Pricing:** Flat monthly action tiers (premium-priced; non-public).
- **Killer feature:** Stealth proxy infra that beats bot detection.
- **Hero copy:** *"AI agents that take actions for you on the web."*
- **Weakness:** Opaque pricing; narrow positioning vs. broad-spectrum Operator.

### Enterprise CX Agents

**11. Sierra (Bret Taylor)** — [sierra.ai](https://sierra.ai)
- **Position:** Outcome-priced enterprise customer-experience agents.
- **User:** F500 CX/Support VPs.
- **Pricing:** ~$150K/yr floor; per-resolution pricing model. $150M ARR.
- **Killer feature:** Outcome-based pricing — only pay when AI resolves.
- **Hero copy:** *"Better customer experiences. Built on Sierra."*
- **Weakness:** Unreachable for SMB; long sales cycles.

- **User:** Mid-market + enterprise CX.
- **Pricing:** ~$50K platform fee + ~$0.99/conversation or ~$0.50/resolution. Median $400K/yr.
- **Killer feature:** Per-resolution billing transparency + agent assist mode.
- **Hero copy:** *"The AI concierge for every customer. Build, optimize, and scale AI agents that treat every customer like the only one."*
- **Weakness:** Same enterprise gating as Sierra; thin SMB story.

- **User:** SMB ops, founders.

- **Hero copy:** *"Scale GTM results, without scaling headcount. The best way to sell with AI."*
- **Weakness:** Narrow to GTM; weaker general dev story.

- **Position:** Multi-agent orchestration framework + enterprise control plane.
- **User:** Devs building agent crews; Fortune 500 platform teams.
- **Pricing:** OSS free (40K+ stars) / AMP starts $99/mo → $120K/yr enterprise.

- **Hero copy:** *"Accelerate AI agent adoption and start delivering production value."*
- **Weakness:** Overhead for simple cases; framework lock-in.

- **User:** Senior AI engineers in production.

- **Killer feature:** Graphs, checkpointing, time-travel debugging.

- **Weakness:** Reputation faded since 2023; quality lags commercial.

- **User:** Technical ops, indie hackers, agencies.
- **Pricing:** Self-hosted free / Cloud Starter ~€20/mo → €800/mo / Enterprise.
- **Killer feature:** Self-hosting + 400+ integrations + native LLM/tool nodes.
- **Hero copy:** *"Secure AI workflow automation."*
- **Weakness:** UX still developer-centric; no native voice/CX layer.

- **User:** Generalist business users.
- **Pricing:** Free 400 activities / Pro 1,500. Stacks on top of Zaps + Copilot + Chatbots.
- **Killer feature:** Largest integration library on earth.
- **Hero copy:** *"AI teammates built for your business."*
- **Weakness:** Add-ons stack to $150–200+/mo fast; weak at long-horizon reasoning.

- **Position:** Developer API for production voice AI agents.
- **User:** Devs building phone agents.
- **Pricing:** $0.05/min platform + LLM/STT/TTS/telephony passthrough → real cost $0.30+/min. Enterprise $3K–$6K/mo.

## Part 2: Synthesis

### 1. Top 5 Hero-Copy Tropes
1. **"AI [job title] for [thing]"** — Devin = "AI software engineer", Vapi = "Voice AI for developers", Sierra/Decagon = "AI concierge". Anthropomorphize the agent into a role.
2. **"Scale [outcome] without scaling headcount"** — Relevance, Lindy, Sierra. The replacement-of-labor pitch.
3. **"Build / Ship / Operate at the speed of thought"** — Cursor, Claude Code, Windsurf. Speed-of-thought productivity pornography.
4. **"Every / autonomous / 24-7 / unattended"** — Manus, Devin, Replit Agent 3. The "set it and forget it" promise.
5. **"Production-grade / reliable / with full control"** — CrewAI, LangGraph, Sierra. Defensive copy aimed at the buyer who got burned by demoware.

### 2. Pricing Patterns
- **Free tier exists at:** OSS frameworks (CrewAI, LangGraph, AutoGPT, n8n), browser/builder tools (Cursor, Windsurf, Manus, Relevance, Zapier). Effectively zero free in pure-play coding agents (Claude Code, Devin) and enterprise CX (Sierra, Decagon).
- **Entry tier sweet spot: $19–$20/mo.** Cursor $20, Devin $20, Claude Pro $20, Manus $20, Relevance $19, Replit Core $20. This is the new "Spotify" anchor for AI prosumers.
- **Power-user tier: $100–$200/mo.** Cursor Ultra $200, Claude Max $100/$200, Lindy Max $199, ChatGPT Pro $200. Designed to capture devs whose company won't reimburse but who personally use it 8h/day.
- **Enterprise floor: $50K–$150K/yr** (Sierra $150K, Decagon ~$50K + usage, CrewAI $120K).
- **Outcome / per-action billing emerging:** Sierra (per-resolution), Decagon (per-conversation/resolution), Replit (effort-based credits), Cursor (credits), Manus (credits), Devin (ACUs). The flat-subscription era is ending.
- **Voice carries an upcharge tax:** Vapi true cost $0.30+/min; Lindy $0.19/min; everyone else lets you bring your own telephony.

### 3. The 3 Biggest White Spaces

**A. Vertical-specific autonomous agents that own a P&L line.**
Everyone sells horizontal "build any agent." Nobody owns *"the agent that runs your wholesaling acquisition pipeline"* or *"the agent that runs your DTC paid-social refresh cycle."* Sierra/Decagon proved verticalizing CX works at $150M ARR — but only one vertical (support). The other 50 verticals are wide open. **You don't sell agents; you sell the result of an agent wired into a specific industry's data + workflows.**

**B. Outcome-priced SMB.**
Sierra invented outcome-based pricing but priced it for F500 ($150K floor). Lindy/Relevance are SMB but flat-subscription. Nobody owns *"$0 if it doesn't close, $X if it does"* for SMB lead-gen, real-estate dispo, e-commerce CRO. This is the next $1B niche. Brock's BDP arms (wholesaling, web, UGC) all map cleanly here.

**C. The "wired-in" / proprietary-data agent.**
Schmidt's thesis is right: model commoditization is real (Opus 4.7 = $5/$25, Sonnet 4.6 = $3/$15, Gemini 3, Manus 1.6 Lite all roughly comparable). Every platform above is a thin orchestration layer over the same 4 model families. **What nobody owns is "agents trained on / wired into private operational data and battle-tested workflows you can't get anywhere else."** That's the moat.

### 4. The Tagline

For a platform whose moat is proprietary BDP workflows + data:

> **"Other agents read the internet. Ours reads your business."**

Backup variants:
- *"Generic agents are a commodity. Ours is wired into the work."*
- *"The agent is the easy part. The workflow is the moat."* (most Schmidt-adjacent)
- *"Built on years of how the work actually gets done."*

The first one wins because it (a) acknowledges the commoditization meta, (b) flips it into a binary positioning ("them vs. us"), (c) implies proprietary data without getting technical, and (d) is short enough to put on a hat.
